# kubernetes_gateway_class_v1

Reads an existing cluster-scoped Gateway API v1 GatewayClass without managing it.

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Optional

- `metadata` (Block List) Standard GatewayClass's metadata. Exactly one metadata block is required. More info: https://github.com/kubernetes/community/blob/master/contributors/devel/sig-architecture/api-conventions.md#metadata (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--metadata))

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Cluster-scoped GatewayClass name.
- `spec` (Attributes List) Observed GatewayClass specification. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--spec))
- `status` (Object) Controller conditions and supported_features. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--status))

<a id="nestedblock--metadata"></a>
### Nested Schema for `metadata`

Required:

- `name` (String) Name of the GatewayClass, must be unique. Cannot be updated. More info: https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/overview/working-with-objects/names/#names

Read-Only:

- `annotations` (Map of String) All observed annotations.
- `generation` (Number) A sequence number representing a specific generation of the desired state.
- `labels` (Map of String) All observed labels, including controller-owned labels.
- `resource_version` (String) An opaque value that represents the internal version of this GatewayClass that can be used by clients to determine when GatewayClass has changed. More info: https://github.com/kubernetes/community/blob/master/contributors/devel/sig-architecture/api-conventions.md#concurrency-control-and-consistency
- `uid` (String) The unique in time and space value for this GatewayClass. More info: https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/overview/working-with-objects/names/#uids

Read-Only:

- `controller_name` (String) Controller identifier.
- `description` (String) Human-readable class description.
- `parameters_ref` (Attributes List) Controller-specific parameters reference. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--spec--parameters_ref))

<a id="nestedatt--spec--parameters_ref"></a>

## Example Usage

```terraform
data "kubernetes_gateway_class_v1" "example" {
  metadata {
    name = "example"
  }
}

output "gateway_class_accepted" {
  description = "Whether the controller accepted the current generation of the GatewayClass."
  value = anytrue([
    for condition in data.kubernetes_gateway_class_v1.example.status.conditions : (
      condition.type == "Accepted" &&
      condition.status == "True" &&
      condition.observed_generation == data.kubernetes_gateway_class_v1.example.metadata[0].generation
    )
  ])
}
```

The output is `true` only when the `Accepted` condition is `True` for the current
`metadata[0].generation`. A condition for an older generation does not describe
the latest spec.

## Behavior notes

- **Prerequisites:** The Gateway API CRDs must be installed. Credentials need
  permission to read cluster-scoped GatewayClasses and API discovery, which the
  provider uses to tell a missing GatewayClass from missing CRDs. The schema
  targets the Gateway API v1.6.3 Standard channel.
- **Missing objects:** Reading a GatewayClass that does not exist is an error;
  the data source never creates it.
- **Lookup by name:** GatewayClass has no namespace. Only `metadata[0].name` is
  configurable; `labels` and `annotations` report every key on the object,
  including controller-managed ones.
- **No waiting:** The lookup does not wait for the controller. Conditions may be
  pending or describe an older generation, and an accepted class does not prove
  that any Gateway or traffic path is operational.
